text.p: Ratings agency Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it had placed Australis Media Ltd's Caa1 senior subordinate rating and its B2 senior secured rating under review, with an uncertain direction.
Moody's said the ratings review affected about US$375 million of debt.

It said the review followed the announcement on Friday of a proposed merger between Australis and fellow pay television operator Foxtel, a joint venture between News Corp Ltd and state-owned telecommunications group Telstra Corp AOT.AX.
"The review will focus upon the benefits that Australis will gain from the merger of Foxtel's broadband network with Australis' satellite and microwave services," Moody's said.
It said the review would also focus on:
* the new capital structure,
* the additional liquidity provided as a result of the recapitalisation of the company,
* Telstra's and News Corp's new funding committments,
* the benefits from the addition of Telstra and News as shareholders,
* and, the likelihood of the merger receiving regulatory approval.

Australis' shares were suspended from trade earlier on Monday at the company's request. Australis said it wanted to give investors time to digest the announcement. Australis closed down half a cent at 18.5 cents on Friday, giving it a market capitalisation of over A$107 million.
Under the deal Australis would effectively acquire Foxtel from Telstra and News in exchange for new shares in Australis.
After the issue of up to 1.66 billion Australis shares, News Corp and Telstra would own up to 66.5 percent of Australis and each appoint three of Australis' 10 directors.
Australis said the merger deal would provide it with additional minimum funding of A$294 million over the next 12 months.
The Australis/Foxtel merger was expected to be completed in November after meeting a number of conditions including due diligence examinations and regulatory approval.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, which rejected an earlier plan to merge Foxtel and Australis, said on Sunday industry conditions had changed since its earlier rejection.
Australis had accumulated losses of A$735 million up to the end of March.
News Corp said the merged entity would trade under the Foxtel name and deliver programming via cable, satelliteaand microwave dish.

The Australian government plans to sell one-third of Telstra later in calendar 1997 and the telecommunications carrier has been under pressure by analysts and fund managers to tidy up its operations ahead of the partial float.
